scope: Same 20 development contexts and fixed STANDARD anchors across all systems

assistant_flagged_standard_cases.1: Off-topic meeting suggestion in response to relief after submitting report.
assistant_flagged_standard_cases.2: Changes supportive eye-appointment conversation into own scheduling conflict.
assistant_flagged_standard_cases.3: Asked which bread; answers fried eggs without addressing bread choice.
assistant_flagged_standard_cases.5: Swaps borrower/lender role: peer offers to return user notes; user offers to return them.
assistant_flagged_standard_cases.6: Claims completed proofreading without prior evidence of completion.
assistant_flagged_standard_cases.7: Contradicts stated inability to play by saying arrival in minutes.
assistant_flagged_standard_cases.9: Asks for notification of overthinking when peer has just reported it.
assistant_flagged_standard_cases.12: Should identify blue sign; instead requests to see it.
assistant_flagged_standard_cases.13: Incoherent location: behind your stand for leaving that same stand.
assistant_flagged_standard_cases.14: Treats distress about unequal workload as a good idea.
assistant_flagged_standard_cases.16: Accepts tonight despite explicitly being busy tonight.
assistant_flagged_standard_cases.17: Requests finding announcement earlier, an impossible backward-time request.
assistant_flagged_standard_cases.18: Responds to gratitude by saying glad peer did not notice; mismatched meaning.

limitations: Assistant issue flags, not human preference labels or calibrated quality ratings.
Unflagged cases are not certified passes.
Can openings include grammatical uses; not a naturalness metric.
Do not compare rates with previous different 30-case review.
Development cases are not untouched test evidence.
